text: Every module of the family is issued as a Draft. The source status 'In review' is not carried forward, because no review or approval of any module version is recorded in the sources and this run takes no human approval step.
why: Template and Rules section R8.1 and the D-RCV-60 overlay: a missing approval is recorded as an assumption and the document continues in Draft status.
read: Root AGENTS.md rule 9 and the D-RCV-60 realignment overlay; the source document control rows 'Status | In review'
applied_in: Document control table, Status row, in all 19 module files; Architecture v5 note, last paragraph
confirm: Business owner approves the module versions at the next requirements review
impact: The module specifications may not be used as an approved baseline until they are signed

text: Every date of the source is copied unchanged, and every release date is read as tentative. The module files carry no release date of their own, so nothing is re-dated and the change-log row of 22 November 2026 is the only new date.
why: Template and Rules U7 and DL48 fix the dates as unchanged and tentative, and a date is never raised as a gap.
read: Template and Rules section R1 (U7) and section R8.1; DL48
applied_in: Document control Date row of every module file, kept at 15 November 2026; Architecture v5 note, closing paragraph
impact: No date moves and no date becomes a gap

text: The family version is the folder (v6 to v7) and each file keeps its own version sequence, so the 18 files at v3 become v4 and the P3 file at v4 becomes v5. The v7 folder holds a copy of every source file next to the new version, as the Technical Specifications by Module v6 folder does.
why: Template and Rules R8.2: a folder family is copied to the next-version folder and only the files that change get a new version inside it. The source family shows file versions that do not follow the folder number (P3 at v4 while the folder is v6).
read: Template and Rules section R8.2; the v5 and v6 folders of the family; 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v6
applied_in: Output file names in the v7 folder
confirm: Document owner confirms the per-file version sequence at the next baseline
impact: A reader finds the source version and the new version side by side in the v7 folder

text: The realignment change of each module file is one Service row in the document control table and one 'Note, Architecture v5 (D-RCV-60)' block. No section, feature, requirement, rule, field, list, message, screen, count or ID is rewritten, and ownership is stated by reference to the Microservice Ownership Map v1 rather than restated section by section.

read: Work package B-REQ-SPEC-27 'Do' and 'Change only what the realignment needs'; Template and Rules section R8.2
